title: HANDOVER: slopvac-lint split, continue here
description:
ANCHOR BEAD. Machine and agent change on 2026-08-17. Read this first, then bd list --status=open.

== WHERE THINGS STAND ==

Branch feat/slopvac-lint-split, 29 commits, PUSHED to origin. Nothing is stranded locally. No PR yet (slopvac-xjb).

Repo: srobroek/slopvac. Package at packages/slopvac-lint/. Dist name, console script, and module are all 'slopvac'.

315 tests pass, exit 0. ruff clean. typos, lychee, markdownlint, taplo all clean locally.

== STANDING USER INSTRUCTIONS (still in force) ==

  Full autonomy to bring the split to end-to-end completion
  i18n-ready spelling, en-US and en-GB
  PyPI publish AUTHORIZED
  CI build-out matching project-scaffold, scanners included in this pass
  Fix issues found rather than only filing them
  Use the write-docs skill for any README/docs/PR/commit text

  SECURITY/LEGAL CONSTRAINT: ASD-STE100 redistribution is scoped. NO verbatim rule
  prose, examples, or wordlist may be redistributed. Rule numbers are cited as
  facts only. Applies to subagent output too.

== HOW TO RUN THINGS ==

From packages/slopvac-lint/ (NOT the repo root -- root ruff config picks up evals/ with different rules):
  uv run --extra dev python -m pytest tests -p no:warnings    # ~5-7 min, EXCEEDS the 120s Bash timeout, use run_in_background
  uvx ruff@0.16.3 check .

GOTCHA: pyproject sets addopts = '-q', so adding -q makes -qq and the summary line vanishes -- the log ends at [100%] with no 'N passed'. Trust the exit code, and count with 'pytest tests --collect-only -q' (should be 315).

From the repo root:
  /tmp/typos .                     (or install typos 1.42.0)
  npx markdownlint-cli2@0.18.1
  uvx taplo@0.9.3 fmt --check
  lizard packages/slopvac-lint/src/slopvac -C 15 -w

Pushing requires 'dgit push' (containerized), NOT 'git push' -- a hook blocks direct github.com pushes.

== WHAT LANDED THIS SESSION ==

  800aadc  clean-room README corpus, brought 37.3 FAIL -> 100.0/100 over nine measured rounds with NO overrides escape hatch
  8a48db5  finish the rename, gate the rules reference with 'slopvac reference --check'
  ede7cdd  rename in the eval harness and the skills
  0a3fee4  track examples/blocklist.toml (referenced by README and pyproject, was untracked)
  fd837ce  a past participle cannot HEAD a noun stack; ruff adoption + python-lint job + gate jobs
  2dedb94  ONE way to disable a category, not two -- see below
  b2e4226  typos/lychee/markdownlint configs and the three real defects they found

== THE CONFIG BUG, FOR CONTEXT ==

2dedb94 was two bugs. CategorySettings.enabled was checked BEFORE severity in Engine._active and no later layer could undo it, so at relaxed a project writing [categories] ste-nouns = 'warning' was silently ignored -- parsed, validated, resolved, changed nothing. Fixing that exposed the same failure one layer down: the profiles stated the disabling twice, as severity='off' AND weight=0.0, so a promoted category inherited the 0.0 and produced findings that could not move the score or fail the run. Weight is now DERIVED from the severity in score_document (score.py:150) and dropped from the 15 profile entries.

Do not reintroduce a second disable mechanism. severity = 'off' is the only one.

== NEXT WORK, IN ORDER ==

  slopvac-sru  P1  wire the four clean checkers into lint.yml   <- start here, lowest risk, configs already committed
  slopvac-xrr  P1  security scanners (NOT probed locally yet, expect triage)
  slopvac-xjb  P1  open the PR
  slopvac-01i  P2  refactor lint (CCN 60) and score_document (CCN 62) below 15 -- user asked for this explicitly
  slopvac-rwg  P2  full-repo dogfood, then flip fail-on-findings to true
  slopvac-tvt  P2  pinact --check and prek
  slopvac-7bh  P2  PyPI publish (blocked on the PR)
  slopvac-dc5  P3  remaining schema items
  slopvac-29e  P3  lizard job (skip if 01i lands first, add gating there instead)
  slopvac-on7  P3  Tengo script checks

== KNOWN NON-ISSUES, DO NOT CHASE ==

  The PostToolUse prose hook reports ~90 ERRORs on .github/workflows/*.yml ('name: Checkout' as ai-tells.ColonUsage, '--' in xargs as an em dash). This is a hook FILE-TYPE SCOPING bug -- a YAML workflow is not consumer prose. The hook lives in agentic-packages, not here. Ignore it on YAML.
  config.py:230 enabled and locale.py LocaleSettings.enabled are DIFFERENT fields and must stay.
  All 27 typos findings were false positives; _typos.toml records why for each class.
  ruff format wants to reformat 24 files. NOT applied on purpose: the rule-provenance comments are this package's documentation and the formatter rewraps them. Offer it, do not assume it.

title: Add pinact --check and prek hooks
description:

title: Refactor cli.py lint and score.py score_document below CCN 15
description:
lizard reports 13 functions in src/slopvac over CCN 15. The two blockers for a gating job are cli.py:450 lint (CCN 60, 203 NLOC, 16 PARAM) and score.py:122 score_document (CCN 62, 160 NLOC). A gating lizard job cannot be added until these come down: threshold 15 fails the build today, threshold 63 can never fire.

Measured baseline (lizard 1.23.0, -C 15):
  compile_vale.py:541 _payload_for CCN 22
  compile_vale.py:953 compile_ruleset CCN 36
  config.py:523 resolve_for CCN 24
  html.py:124 render_html CCN 27
  rules.py:86 _verify_examples CCN 16
  vale.py:59 run_compiled_vale CCN 21
  engine.py:703 _run_lexical CCN 17
  engine.py:761 _run_metric CCN 39
  engine.py:1037 document_metric CCN 28
  cli.py:72 _collect_paths CCN 16
  cli.py:450 lint CCN 60
  cli.py:745 list_rules CCN 17
  cli.py:827 explain CCN 18

Extraction shape, not an arbitrary split: lint carries the config-explain block, the blocklist load, and the per-format reporting branches, each separable. score_document computes three densities (raw/gating/weighted) plus per-category aggregation in one pass.

Guarded by 315 passing tests. Wants its own commit and a full green run.

title: Prune the slopvac compile cache
description:
~/.cache/slopvac/ accumulates one directory per ruleset fingerprint and never removes any. Observed: 209 directories, 83M, on a single development machine. Each ruleset edit, severity change, profile change, or blocklist edit mints a new key, so the growth is proportional to development activity rather than to use.

No correctness impact -- the fingerprint check means a stale entry is never served -- but it is unbounded disk growth in a user cache directory.

Options: prune by mtime on compile (keep the N most recent), or a 'slopvac cache prune' subcommand, or both.
close_reason: Both options implemented in 90d177f: LRU prune to CACHE_KEEP=16 on every compile that owns the shared cache (mtime refreshed on cache hit, so use beats recency of build), plus a 'slopvac cache' subcommand with --prune and --all. 209 trees/83M -> 16/1.0MiB. Documented in README.

title: Evaluate Vale script checks (Tengo) for genre structure rules
description:
Vale's `extends: script` check runs a Tengo script over the document and can
assert on structure, not just on token patterns. Verified with vale 3.15.2 during
the 2026-07-27 style audit: a script check reporting "consumer doc has no
'## Install' heading" fires at 1:1 on a document that lacks it.

Every rule slopvac ships is a regex over prose. That reaches wording and misses
shape, so the gate cannot tell a README with no install section from one that has
three, or catch an ADR with a Decision heading and no Consequences. The
`write-docs` skill states its genre rules in prose and nothing enforces them.

## What a script check can reach

- required headings per genre (consumer: Install, Usage; ADR: Context, Decision,
  Consequences; CONTRIBUTING: how to run the tests)
- heading order and nesting depth
- a fenced code block with no language tag
- a link with no target
- a table whose header count and row cell counts disagree
- section length ratios: a section padded to match a sibling

## Why this is not done yet

The mechanism is the easy half. The hard half is deciding what each genre MUST
contain, and that is a house position rather than a measurement. Getting it wrong
produces a rule that fires on every document a project already has, which is how
a gate gets switched off.

Blocked on that decision, not on the mechanism.
design:
A new style, `prose-genre`, one rule per structural assertion, all at warning.

Mechanism, verified with vale 3.15.2:

    extends: script
    message: "%s"
    level: warning
    scope: raw
    script: |
      text := import("text")
      matches := []
      if !text.contains(scope, "## Install") {
        matches = append(matches, {begin: 0, end: 1,
          message: "consumer doc has no '## Install' heading"})
      }

`scope: raw` hands the script the whole document. The `matches` array is what
Vale reports, and each entry needs `begin`, `end`, and `message`. Reporting at
0:1 anchors the finding to the top of the file, which is right for a
whole-document assertion: there is no line to point at when the defect is an
absence.

Routing follows the genre sections already in `vale.ini.template`. A required
heading for a consumer README is wrong for a commit message, so each rule is
scoped to the genre it belongs to rather than switched off everywhere else.

Open questions to settle before writing rules:

- Which headings are genuinely required per genre, and which are conventions this
  project happens to like? Anything in the second group does not ship.
- Does the assertion belong in Vale at all, or in the `review-docs` judgement
  pass? Vale gives determinism and a file:line; the skill gives reasons. A
  missing Install section is mechanical, so Vale. "The heading promises something
  the section withholds" is not, so the skill.
- Tengo has no filesystem access, so a relative-link check cannot verify the path
  exists. That one needs a script outside Vale.
acceptance_criteria:
A decision recorded either way.

If adopted: a prose-genre style with per-genre structural rules, each with a
fixture proving it fires on an absence and stays quiet on a conforming document,
routed through the existing genre sections in vale.ini.template, and picked up by
gen-rule-table.py.

If rejected: the reason written down so the next style audit does not re-derive
the mechanism from scratch.
